name: Malia Cohen
title: California State Controller; Democratic candidate for re-election (2026)
years_of_service: San Francisco Board of Supervisors (District 10) 2011 to 2019, president 2018 to 2019; Board of Equalization (District 2) 2019 to 2023; State Controller since January 2, 2023. (Wikipedia)
background: Cohen was born December 16, 1977, in San Francisco. She holds a bachelor's degree in political science from Fisk University and a graduate degree from Carnegie Mellon. She worked on Gavin Newsom's 2003 mayoral campaign and in his mayoral office. (Wikipedia)

She represented District 10 on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors from 2011 to 2019, sponsoring the city's large-capacity magazine limit and co-authoring its Fair Chance ("ban the box") ordinance, and was board president in 2018 to 2019. She then served on the Board of Equalization (2019 to 2023). (Wikipedia)

She won the 2022 Controller race with 55.35% over Republican Lanhee Chen and placed first in the June 2026 primary with 56.80%. In October 2026 a federal lawsuit alleged that her office's unclaimed-property contractors took and sold foreign investors' assets without adequate notice; these are allegations, not findings. (Wikipedia)
